newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt new issue frenzy continues, more seen.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt new issue frenzy continues, more seen.

text.p: Despite Thursday's corporate debt new issue frenzy, another barrage of issues is set to come to market, as the recent emergence of capital securities offerings triggers an avalanche of 144A deals, dealers said.
On Thursday about $2.0 billion in new investment grade debt was priced in the corporate bond primary market with another $1.5 billion in the private placement.
However, dealers said a growing trend is emerging among a differently structured security which has come to market quietly but by the boatload in just the last four days.

Market sources noted that these types of deals had not been seen earlier. But since Tuesday the market has been deluged with close to 15 issues, with some issuers seen bringing multiple offerings to market within this short period.
"There weren't any of these issues before... but since Tuesday we've seen about 15 deals," a syndicate source said.

"There's such little information out on them, some people call them trust capital securities, others preferred bank securities...it seems everybody has their own little names for them," the source added.

Among issues this week alone were: Wells Fargo's $300 million and $200 million deals, Barnett Bank's $200 million and $300 million deals, Republic Bank of NY's $150 million, Bank of Boston's $200 million, Bankers Trust's $250 million, First Chicago's $300 million, Allstate's $200 million, Conseco's $325 million, First Union's $500 million, Countrywide's $300 million and BankAmerica's $450 milllion deal, syndicate sources added.
Comerica is expected to tap the market with its own deal as early as Friday, sources added.

"The bottom line...is that people are doing these (deals) because it doesn't hurt their balance sheet," said one syndicate source. "It's treated like equity on their balance sheet so it doesn't hurt any of their ratios, for instance debt to equities, he added.
Separately, another $1.5 billion was priced in the 144A private placement debt arena on Thursday, dealers said.

Among those 144A debt issues were: Newport News Shipbuilding's $400 million, Tevecap SA's $250 million, HS Resources' $150 million, Eastern Energy Ltd's $350 million, Omnipoint's $200 million and Statia Terminals' $135 million.

Among Thursday's investment grade deals were: Commercial Credit's $200 million, Circus Circus Enterprises' $300 million, Enersis SA's $800 million, Peoples Bank Corp's $150 million and Simon DeBartolo's $200 million.
In addition, $1.0 billion in eurobond debt was brought to market by Russia on Thursday in a successful debut offering.
Dealers said overall deals were well received by the market and many issues were bumped up in size to meet investor demand.
In new issue secondary trading, Circus Circus Enterprises new 40-year and 100-year bonds were seen widening when freed to trade, sources said.
"Circus Circus' new issues were seen wider on the break," one dealer said.
Meanwhile, as the torrent of issuance continues, Millennium America tapped the market on Friday with a $750 million two-part debt offering via Goldman Sachs & Co.
The $500 million 7.00 percent 10-year notes were priced to yield 88 basis points over Treasuries and the $250 million 7.625 percent debentures priced to yield 88 basis points.
Also, WCI Steel priced $300 million in 144A 10-year senior secured notes to yield 10 percent, syndicate sources said.
Still, ABN Amro Bank NV is expected to issue $300 million in AA2/AA-minus rated 30-year debt, sources said.
TransContinental Gas Pipeline is also expected to bring $200 million in 30-year debt.
Among upcoming 144A offerings are Atrium Co's $100 million 10-year senior note deal and Clark Material Handling's $120 million in 10-year senior notes.
--Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675
